title: How Legora is transforming the legal workspace using Azure OpenAI Service
author: Microsoft

dom.t: Legora partnerships: Adoption needs selected workflows and training

st.t: Legora partnerships: Adoption needs selected workflows and training
st.an: The source supports Legora’s platform-led adoption narrative by presenting selected legal workflows, familiar Microsoft integrations and Azure compliance infrastructure as adoption enablers. It also aligns with the cluster’s caution that deployment and promotional speed claims do not independently establish accuracy, legal-work quality or client outcomes.
qs: Key to its success is the ease with which Legora integrates with Word and SharePoint, meaning thousands of lawyers can now extract information, run reviews, and perform research across legal information and precedents safely, using Legora.
And by grounding Legora's responses in the underlying material, verifying the AI’s thinking and output is simpler than ever.

kp.k: Legal AI workspace augments lawyers across text-intensive tasks
kp.d: Microsoft's 2025 customer story presents Legora, formerly Leya, as a legal technology platform assisting thousands of lawyers with contract review, due diligence and legal research. CEO Max Junestrand frames the product as an intelligent colleague enhancing legal professionals' capabilities, rather than replacing them.
qs: Legora acts as an AI-powered workspace and has been adapted to better understand the intricacies of legal work—serving as an intelligent colleague to every legal professional,
Since then, they have assisted thousands of lawyers from some of the best-known firms in the world in tackling specific tasks and the text-intensive work that lawyers handle daily.
Starting with jobs such as contract review, due diligence, and legal research, they built a single platform designed to solve and simplify them.

kp.k: Parallel document extraction promises substantial task-level time savings
kp.d: The story claims automation reduces some tasks from hours to minutes, and Tabular Review reduces document extraction from hours to seconds through tens of thousands of parallel model calls. Applications include loan portfolios, leases and transaction agreements. These are product-performance claims; the document supplies no timed study, sample size or comparative measurement methodology.
qs: What used to take hours of manual labor can now be automated in a few minutes.

Transforming hours of manual work into seconds, Tabular Review fires off tens of thousands of parallel calls to extract terms or answers in documents, enhancing legal-specific tasks such as loan portfolio analyses, lease agreements, Share purchase agreement, limited partnership agreements, master services agreements, and more.

kp.k: Grounding and retrieval support verification and multi-document work
kp.d: The story says grounding responses in source material simplifies verification of AI output. It describes multi-agentic behavior, retrieval-augmented generation and parallel API calls as enabling complex queries and reviews across documents, with larger output windows. It does not report measured accuracy or hallucination rates.
qs: And by grounding Legora's responses in the underlying material, verifying the AI’s thinking and output is simpler than ever.
To this end, Legora uses various technologies, such as multi-agentic behavior, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), and large-scale parallelization of API calls to the LLMs.

These intelligent assistants facilitate complex queries and reviews across multiple documents, using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) techniques to provide precise and context-aware insights—allowing for significantly larger output windows than traditional alternatives.

kp.k: Microsoft integrations embed AI within existing legal workflows
kp.d: The story attributes adoption partly to integration with Word and SharePoint, allowing lawyers to extract information, review documents and research precedents. Word integration supports review and annotation, redline summaries and issues lists within familiar workflows, which the story claims reduces disruption.
qs: Key to its success is the ease with which Legora integrates with Word and SharePoint, meaning thousands of lawyers can now extract information, run reviews, and perform research across legal information and precedents safely, using Legora.

Embedding AI capabilities directly into Microsoft Word allows lawyers to review and annotate documents within their familiar workflow, reducing disruptions and fostering seamless adoption and use-cases such as summarization of redlines, creation of issues lists, and more.

kp.k: Confidentiality requirements shape infrastructure choices and customer selection
kp.d: Junestrand says Legora moved from direct OpenAI APIs to Azure OpenAI Service because clients required a more robust security, compliance, privacy and confidentiality solution. Separately, Bird & Bird's Hélder Santos attributes his firm's selection of Legora after evaluating alternatives to security and compliance alongside its technological ambition. These are executive and customer accounts carried by Microsoft, rather than independent compliance findings.
qs: In the first weeks, we used OpenAI’s APIs directly, but quickly it became evident that for our clients—where security, compliance, data privacy, and confidentiality are paramount—we needed a more robust long-term solution,
With Azure OpenAI Service, we can offer those secure and compliant AI solutions.

We evaluated several alternatives on the market and chose Legora as our trusted AI partner because of their unquestionable focus on security and compliance combined with the ambition and drive to equip our lawyers with the best technology available,

kp.k: Regional deployment supports international scaling and data residency
kp.d: The story reports Legora serves hundreds of law firms, financial institutions and multinational corporations across 16 countries, naming Bird & Bird, Mannheimer Swartling and Pérez-Llorca among clients. It attributes international scalability partly to Azure's regional model deployment and local data residency compliance. CTO Sigge Labor also identifies trust in Microsoft's security framework as supporting expansion.
qs: Legora´s rapid growth—from startup to global player serving hundreds of law firms, financial institutions, and multinational corporations across 16 countries—is significantly bolstered by its strategic partnership with Microsoft.
Using Azure’s scalable infrastructure, Legora can deploy AI models regionally, ensuring a critical factor in the legal industry: compliance with local data residency laws.
Our clients trust Microsoft, and by extension, they trust us to handle their sensitive data with the utmost care.

kp.k: Future development prioritizes deeper ecosystem integration
kp.d: The story states that Legora plans deeper Microsoft ecosystem integrations. Junestrand presents continued AI development and integration with lawyers' everyday tools as a means to rethink high-quality legal work. This is a strategic ambition, not a demonstrated future outcome or a dated implementation commitment.
qs: Looking ahead, Legora will continue to explore deeper integrations within the Microsoft ecosystem.
Our goal is not just to keep pace with technological advancements but to lead the way in rethinking what it means to perform high-quality legal work,
By staying at the forefront of AI development and integrating seamlessly with tools that lawyers use daily, we’re setting new standards for what legal technology can achieve.

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: Microsoft’s customer story claims that Legora automates text-intensive legal tasks, reducing hours of work to minutes or, for document extraction, seconds.
pts.d: The narrative describes contract review, due diligence and legal research as current applications. It attributes Tabular Review’s speed to tens of thousands of parallel model calls extracting terms and answers across documents, including loan portfolios, leases and transaction agreements. These are task-level efficiency claims, not explicit predictions of lawyer replacement or changes to legal employment.

pts.k: The story claims that grounding and retrieval make AI assistance more context-aware and easier for lawyers to verify.
pts.d: The narrative links grounding in underlying documents to easier human checking of AI reasoning and output. It describes multi-agentic behavior and retrieval-augmented generation as supporting complex, multi-document queries and reviews, with larger output windows than unspecified traditional alternatives. CEO Max Junestrand frames the product as an intelligent colleague that enhances lawyers’ capabilities rather than an autonomous substitute.

pts.k: Integration into familiar Microsoft applications is claimed to reduce workflow disruption and facilitate adoption.
pts.d: The narrative says Word and SharePoint integration lets lawyers extract information, review documents and research legal information and precedents safely. Within Word, claimed applications include annotation, redline summarization and issues-list creation. The proposed mechanism is embedding AI in tools lawyers already use rather than requiring a separate workflow.

pts.k: Junestrand and CTO Sigge Labor claim that Azure’s security and infrastructure enable compliant legal AI deployment and international expansion.
pts.d: Junestrand says Legora moved from direct OpenAI API use to Azure OpenAI Service to address clients’ confidentiality, privacy, security and compliance requirements. The narrative links regional model deployment to compliance with local data residency laws. Labor attributes expansion partly to Azure’s global reach and clients’ trust in Microsoft. These claims concern infrastructure and handling sensitive legal information, rather than demonstrated improvement in substantive legal advice.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The evidence offered consists of product descriptions, reported adoption and executive and customer testimony, without a documented performance study.
pts.d: The story reports thousands of lawyer users and hundreds of client organizations across 16 countries, and names Bird & Bird, Mannheimer Swartling and Pérez-Llorca. Bird & Bird’s Hélder Santos reports evaluating alternatives and selecting Legora for security, compliance and its technology ambitions; he does not supply measured productivity results. The hours-to-minutes/seconds, verification and precision claims have no accompanying task samples, benchmark methods, accuracy figures or quantified verification costs. Technical descriptions of RAG and parallel calls provide an asserted mechanism, not a measured comparison.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: Most benefits are presented as already occurring in the 2025 story; deeper integration and leadership in legal technology are future ambitions without deadlines.
pts.d: Current claims depend on the described Azure-based platform, source grounding, RAG, parallel processing, access to multiple recent models and integration with existing applications. Security and confidentiality are presented as prerequisites for client adoption, while regional deployment supports local data residency requirements. Looking ahead, the narrative anticipates deeper Microsoft integrations, and Junestrand expresses an ambition to redefine high-quality legal work. No dated rollout, forecast of adoption rates or timeline for profession-wide transformation is provided.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The claimed beneficiaries are lawyers and legal teams in law firms and enterprise organizations, with Legora benefiting through scalable international distribution.
pts.d: Lawyers are described as gaining faster document-intensive workflows, easier verification and AI assistance within familiar software. Law firms, financial institutions and multinational corporations are the reported customer base, with security and local data residency emphasized for organizations handling sensitive information. Legora is a legal-technology vendor supplying a workspace, not described as an alternative legal service provider delivering legal work. The source offers no concrete claims about staffing structures, junior-lawyer displacement, fees or access to justice for underserved individuals.
